questions.question: How were the four persona briefs actually written — real device and job constraints, or just demographic labels with a task attached?
questions.why: The speaker credits the panel with catching a usability failure but only describes Dez in one line, so the method behind the briefs is unclear.

questions.question: Dez's task time went from 30 seconds to 9, simulated — do you treat that as a usability number at all, or only as a proxy until a human confirms it?
questions.why: The notes flag it as simulated, not human, which is exactly the kind of AI-user-research number this persona distrusts.

questions.question: Once the personas walk a live browser and say DONE or NOT, who on the team actually turns that verdict into a design decision, and can anyone decline what the panel asks for?
questions.why: The talk never names a person who owns design judgment between the panel's verdict and the merge.

questions.question: After moving to a live browser and three widths, what specifically did the next panel catch before merge, beyond your own sense that things got better?
questions.why: The speaker admits the improvement is unmeasured, only 'in my experience,' which invites a follow-up on actual evidence.

questions.question: What changed on the labeler review screen itself that cut your review time from three minutes to 20 to 30 seconds, and was that redesign tested on anyone besides you?
questions.why: The speaker credits a 'persona-driven redesign' of the review screen but shows no before/after of the screen or evidence beyond his own stopwatch.

questions.question: When the scout was flapping, what did that actually look like to someone watching the stream — did you observe a real user's reaction, or only your own instrumented session?
questions.why: Flapping is framed as a technical defect via a chart, but the human experience of it on a real screen is never described.

questions.question: Is the persona panel meant to replace hands-on usability testing with real people, or only to feed and prioritize it — where's that line for you?
questions.why: The talk positions the panel as the 'done' gate without saying whether real user research still happens afterward.

questions.question: The 65 percent top-3 figure on live auctions is your own taps over five days — do you have a plan to validate that with other users before calling it a usable rate?
questions.why: The speaker flags this as his own single-person sample, which is thin evidence for a headline usability claim.

questions.question: Before the phone test caught it, did anyone actually hold a device while building the UI, or was 'done' judged entirely on the fixed-size panel screens?
questions.why: The gap between panel-DONE and phone-unusable suggests no one held a real device until the morning after.

questions.question: For the crop-versus-vote decision that fixed misidentified cards, was that judged only by replaying recordings, or did a person watch it live on a real stream before it shipped?
questions.why: The demo frames this as an experiment result, but the actual on-device verification of that behavior change is left out.
